rows.title: [Mid (6-11)] [Early (0-5)] Saw younger brother in high chair
rows.description: saw my younger brother in high  chair.  He was feeding himself.  I was glad I was going into the garden to play
rows.sageEnrichment: The client found satisfaction in this memory because it represented the possibility of leaving the table and going off to play on his own, signifying a feeling of freedom and independence compared to his younger brother who was confined to his high chair.

rows.title: [Early (0-5)] children's christmas party
rows.description: My sister and I went to my father's company christmas party.  I rememember dark wood, warmth and "posh" presents
rows.sageEnrichment: The client found the children's Christmas party satisfying because it felt like a 'real grown-up' event, and he experienced a sense of belonging and deserving to be there.

rows.title: [Mid (6-11)] [Early (0-5)] children's christmas party
rows.description: My sister and I went to my father's company christmas party.  I rememeber dark wood, warmth and "posh" presents
rows.sageEnrichment: The client found the children's Christmas party satisfying because it felt like a 'real grown-up' event, and he experienced a sense of belonging and deserving to be there.

rows.title: [Mid (6-11)] [Early (0-5)] Going to school
rows.description: remeber first day.  I was worried that I didn't have my sports kit - in case we'd be doing sports.  we didn't, and I remember my relief.
rows.sageEnrichment: The client's satisfaction from his first day of school came from the profound relief of not needing sports kit, which he associated with having already done enough to perform, rather than from the act of going to school itself.

rows.title: [Mid (6-11)] [Early (0-5)] Can't remeber anything else
rows.description: I have very few early memories

rows.title: [Early (0-5)] Can't remmeber anything else
rows.description: I have very few early memories

rows.title: Set up Business
rows.description: Habing left the Army I decided to set up my own buinsess.  I had worked for 18 months in a law firm, so decided to focus on lawyers.  Initaially worked with a collegaue, but we parted on good terms.  Business was good, and work was enjoyable,

rows.title: Bought current house
rows.description: We decided to move house - open to where.  Decided that betwen our respective parents made sense.  saw house and agreed that it was both far too big yet just what we wanted.  Waited over  a year for it to complete, but increasingly knew it was right.

rows.title: helped found church
rows.description: The church we joined on arrival in our new home broke up.  WE helped found a new church, with one of the previous homegroup leaders.  Enjoyed the sense of calling, plus the possibility of creating something "that worked"

rows.title: Took holidays
rows.description: For much of my life we had been unable to take holidays with just my wife and I.  We decided that this should change, and went for a break to Gambia.

rows.title: Started fostering
rows.description: Had often considered fostering.  decided this was the right moment to persue it.  Got 2 young girls who have remained family memebrs for 17 years!

rows.title: Kept on paying the mortgage
rows.description: The 2008 recession changed many people's business. Mine took a hit, but we continued to pay very large mortgage payments.

rows.title: new foster daughter arrived
rows.description: Poppy arrived as a very sick two and a half year old. We had to fight very hard to keep her., Which led to a variety of interventions with government at different levels. we eventually won.

rows.title: Coaching MA
rows.description: I had been coaching since 2006. I decided it was a good opportunity to find more detail about the structure of coaching, rather than the practice. Over two years part-time I dug into the theory behind what I was doing, I discovered various other ways of doing it.

rows.title: Took Fridays off
rows.description: For many years I promised that I would work a four-day week. I finally decided to take Fridays off and have managed to keep that time free. This enables my wife and I to spend time together in what is otherwise a full-time 365-day-a-year job.

rows.title: Kept learning.
rows.description: When AI arrived I took the opportunity to learn what could be done with it and how I could use it to leverage what I do . I rebuilt my business on the back of AI, via live work and AI scenarios.

rows.title: Decided to become Shared Life Cares
rows.description: Decided to use the cottage attached to our house (which was previously occupied by my son and daughter-in-law) to house people who could otherwise not live alone. The processes aren't just tedious but fundamentally worthwhile.

rows.title: thinking of retirement
rows.description: I'm pondering what I would do if I wasn't working with clients.  I like earning money, but it's not a driver

messages: 9	[Mid (6-11)] PLAYED BOARD GAMES	My brother Richard and | discovered that we liked Board games. We set out to collect as
many as possible - through school fetes, presents, swapping or whatever. We both enjoyed
learning new rules, understanding how to win and then finding new games. Discovered that

some games that looked good were unplayable.	7	childhood	The client found the process of playing board games satisfying because it allowed him and his brother the creative freedom to adapt and improve upon the original designs, making the games better and continuously engaging them by avoiding boredom.	satisfying
10	[Mid (6-11)] LED GANG	Lived on estate. | wanted to play war, but was bored with usual rules. Designed system of
buying and selling guns, prizes and events so that the “war” could have some long-term
significance. | acted as banker, and sometimes led one of the sides. We pooled our
weapons so that we could “buy” the good ones if we wanted. The scheme lasted most of

the summer until we went back to school.	8	childhood	The client found leading the gang enjoyable because he created a system and process that delivered the desired result and provided a continuous, engaging experience for others, transforming a short-term activity into something with long-term significance.	enjoyable
11	[Mid (6-11)] PASSED 11+	A friend of mine - with pushy middle class parents - was sent to private school because his
parents thought he would fail 11+. He was seen as much cleverer than me, so there was
huge delight (for me plus parents) when | passed the 11+. The school were surprised - they
had been preparing me for the comprehensive. Father was so pleased he went out and

bought me a grammar school cap, even though nobody wore them!	8	childhood	The client found passing the 11+ exam both satisfying and fulfilling; satisfying because it brought joy to his parents despite his academic history, and fulfilling because it shifted his self-perception, making him realize he was cleverer than he thought.	fulfilling
12	[Mid (6-11)] WON FOOTBALL CUP	Asked to play for the cubs newly-formed football team. Big for age, so played centre-half.
Few talented players, but very committed. Often lost in league matches but gained winning-
streak in cup. Enjoyed winning as part of team. Enjoyed seeing the reaction in our

managers face when we collected the medals.	9	childhood	The client found winning the football cup satisfying not for his individual skill, but for the surprise and delight of the collective achievement for himself, the team, and the manager, especially given his role in organizing matches for others.	satisfying
14	[Late (12-18)] LEARNED BRIDGE	Three card brag had become boring. Saw people playing bridge and wanted to learn.
Quickly discovered it was modified whist, and became good at the card-play, developing the bidding system more slowly. Took books from library to understand the bidding, but

never had regular partner, so card-playing remained my strenth.	13	teens	The client found learning Bridge satisfying due to the combination of fixed rules and the element of chance, where his growing knowledge and skill could significantly improve his chances of winning within a structured yet unpredictable environment.	satisfying
13	[Late (12-18)] WARGAMING	Tried to make models, but discovered it was difficult to make them look good. Instead
bought small tanks - could be painted just one colour - and began to wargame, starting with
the simple rules - Donald Featherstone - and then moving to more complex rules. Played
with close friends, usually WW2. | had a mixed force, so we could sort out sides when we

played. Aim was to have a good, balanced fight, not just win.	13	teens	The client found wargaming satisfying because it allowed him to experiment with different rules and armies, focusing on playability and ensuring the game was enjoyable and balanced for both sides, rather than just winning.	satisfying
15	[Late (12-18)] BECAME CHRISTIAN	Mother died when 13. She wanted us all to get confirmed. Went to confirmation classes,
and after service was asked if | wanted to play football. Said yes and ended up in
Pathfinders Class. After a couple of years | was asked if | was a Christian and said | didn't

know. Was led to Christ. Didn't feel much different, thought | now belonged in	15	teens	The client found becoming a Christian fulfilling because it led to the discovery of a larger purpose that transcended day-to-day existence, offering a more profound hope for the future.	fulfilling
16	[Late (12-18)] WELBECK EXAM	Travelled alone to two-day assessment centre for Army 6th Form College - Welbeck.
Enjoyed the various tasks and written exams. Met many new people, all of whom| liked.
Wondered who else would be joining me at Welbeck, even though | hadn't yet been

accepted. Had supreme confidence despite mediocre academic record to that date.	16	teens	The client found the Welbeck exam fulfilling due to a combination of the independence he experienced in traveling there alone and the sense of achievement in being selected, an outcome unexpected by his peers.	fulfilling
17	SANDHURST - PUBLIC SPEAKING	Sandhurst was difficult. Required physical fitness | barely had. Got trench-foot and back-
squadded. Suddenly blossomed when required to do presentation on Yom Kippur War.
Gave electrifying performance - Colour Sergeant and all the platoon were awestruck “best

they'd ever heard”. The way people saw me changed - or was it my perception?	19	twenties	The client found satisfaction in his public speaking experience at Sandhurst due to the short and immediate feedback loop he received from the audience, directly observing their response to his words.	satisfying
18	royal engineers acceptance	The Royal Engineers were the hardest Corp to gain entry to. Having been to Welbeck there
was a strict quota, and the word on the street was “you have to be an excellent junior officer to get in" -
I wasn't.  went to the interview convinced that they should want me - | remember being
very confident, and enjoyed the tough questioning. | got the result | expected, and excelled

in the Academic part of Sandhurst that followed	20	twenties	The client found gaining acceptance into the Royal Engineers satisfying because it represented the achievement of a difficult, self-imposed goal, especially given his less-than-spectacular Sandhurst record.	satisfying
19	LED Christian union	Ran Christian Union at Military University. Decided to forgo the standard pragrammed
activities in favour of small-group gatherings and intimate worship. Not universally
welcomed (one of the professors stopped coming)) but it created the Christian Union |

wanted. We became closer as a group, and began to understand one another.	22	twenties	The client found leading the Christian Union fulfilling because he transformed it from a standard, pre-programmed schedule into something dynamic and responsive, allowing it to evolve rather than being fixed in advance.	fulfilling
20	MARRIED	Knew that | was meant to be married to Desiree. Asking her was just a formality - | knew
that she would say “yes”. She understood me without me having to explain, and delighted
in being with me. | found delight in making her happy, and she took great pains to reinforce

my self confidence. | never doubted that she loved me more than her family, even though	26	twenties	The client found getting married fulfilling due to the profound experience of being adored and deeply valued by someone he perceived as superior to him in many ways, finding powerful affirmation and love despite his own self-assessment.	fulfilling
21	bought first computer	Owned electric typewriter but realised that computers were the way ahead. Spent £600
buying computer from Peter Daws. Taught myself DOS, Word processing, databases etc.
Continued to upgrade equipment, determined to ensure that | was always “ahead of the

curve” when compared to my contemporaries.	NULL	thirties	The client found buying and mastering his first computer satisfying because the new technology empowered him to perform tasks independently that previously would have required him to travel to a central computer.	satisfying
22	MBA	First (and only?) Army Officer to be sponsored to do MBA at LBS. To attend required
extensive negotiations with Military Survey, and completing it meant writing essays in the
back of an armoured vehicle during the Gulf War. The MBA taught me the power of good
questions, and that if | don't understand something there's a good chance it's the fault of
the explainer! It gave me a specialism and a world-view that none of my contemporaries

had, and lead to a range of jobs which would have otherwise been beyond me.	31	thirties	The client found undertaking his MBA fulfilling because it led to a profound realization that demystified the business world, specifically discovering that individuals he had previously perceived as 'omnipotent' were not infallible.	fulfilling
23	gulf war	Posted to 1 Armoured Division as geographic officer. Discovered that | really could do the
job I'd been trained for. Much had to be invented as we went along, and | had responsibility
for both the map supply and terrain analysis for the division. Despite the plans constantly
changing | always succeeding in getting the maps to the units as required - a huge

logistical exercise.	32	thirties	The client found his Gulf War experience satisfying because it affirmed his capability and competence in the specific role he had been trained for, even if he didn't always enjoy being a soldier.	satisfying
24	left army	After many houses in 11 years of marriage decided to leave Army. Planned it meticulously,
first moving Church, then moving out of Army accommodation before finally moving jobs.
Spent previous year being trained by Wilsher Group to become excellent coach and
facilitator, so left Army confident of way ahead. Left completely - no Regimental ties - to
ensure that | became a real civilian.	37	thirties	NULL	fulfilling
